title: Bram and the Oath
premise: Bram Winterbourne, called Quentin by the crown's records, has spent his life as keeper of the Hollow Gate in a valley where magic cannot follow—until a royal decree orders the hunting of all gifted folk, and the gate he guards begins to whisper his true name. Fleeing with the gate's last key, Bram discovers the valley sits inside Aldermere, a country erased from maps and memory, and that the door out exists only for those who remember it whole. Hunted by a truth-reader inquisitor and betrayed by the friend who reported him, Bram must choose between sealing the valley forever to save its people and opening the gate to restore a nation the crown buried. In the end he opens it, sacrificing his own memories of the valley, so that Aldermere—and he, as a stranger to it—can exist again.
about_author: Cyrus Ravensworth is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing border-town records before turning to fiction. They write quiet fantasies about forgotten places, drawn from a childhood spent between two villages that no longer appear on any map.

chapters.title: The Keeper of Hollow Gate
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. We meet the valley where magic cannot follow, Bram's quiet routine as gatekeeper, and his unspoken gift that has never once worked inside the borders. When a crown courier arrives posting a decree—the hunt for the gifted begins at midwinter—Bram realizes his name is on a list he never knew existed. Emotional beat: the comfort of smallness curdling into dread.

chapters.title: A Name in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Searching the gatehouse archives, Bram finds his own entry: 'Quentin Winterbourne, keeper, born outside.' He has no memory of anywhere else. His oldest friend, Tam, notices the missing pages and asks too many questions. Bram lies for the first time in his life. Emotional beat: the vertigo of discovering your own history has been edited.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Coach
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Bram and Serah Vane, the crown's truth-reader, who can taste lies like copper. Serah arrives in the valley, frustrated that her gift fails at the border. She interviews Bram, who tells the truth and is believed—until Tam, terrified, hints at the ledger. Emotional beat: the horror that honesty offers no protection when the questions are wrong.

chapters.title: What the Gate Whispers
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The Hollow Gate begins speaking to him at night, calling him by a name that isn't his and showing him fragments: a city of brass bells, a woman singing, a door in a hillside. His gift, dormant for thirty years, flickers to life only at the gate's threshold. Emotional beat: longing—he has never wanted anything until now.

chapters.title: Tam's Choice
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Torn between love for Bram and fear for his own family, Tam reports the ledger to Serah, believing Bram will only be questioned. Serah orders the valley sealed and Bram taken at dawn. Tam realizes too late that 'questioned' means the truth-reader's rack of memories. Emotional beat: guilt arriving ahead of its consequences.

chapters.title: Flight Across the Borderline
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, with Serah in pursuit. Bram steals the gate's iron key and crosses the valley border for the first time—magic floods him, painful and glorious, and the erased country of Aldermere shimmers into half-existence around him. Serah follows, her gift returning too, and for a moment they are two gifted people in a ghost nation. Emotional beat: wonder shadowed by pursuit.

chapters.title: The Country That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. In half-real Aldermere, Bram meets the Remnant—people erased with their country, sustained by shared memory, dying a little more each year as the crown's forgetting spreads. Their elder reveals the truth: the gate can restore Aldermere, but only a keeper who remembers the valley can open it, and opening it will take those memories as payment. Emotional beat: the weight of a price hidden in a promise.

chapters.title: The Truth-Reader's Doubt
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Cornering Bram at the door in the hillside, Serah reads him—and instead of lies finds a lifetime of honest smallness and one enormous secret: the crown itself ordered Aldermere erased, and Serah's own childhood memories have been trimmed. Her certainty cracks. She lets Bram reach the door. Emotional beat: loyalty to the crown breaking against loyalty to truth.

chapters.title: The Oath at the Door
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Climax. At the threshold, the gate demands its price: every memory of the valley, of Tam, of the life he built. Tam arrives, having defected, and begs him not to pay it—offering instead to take half the cost. Together they swear the old oath, splitting the loss, and Bram turns the key as Serah holds the crown's riders back. Emotional beat: sacrifice transformed by shared burden.

chapters.title: A Stranger in Aldermere
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, coda. Aldermere is whole again, brass bells ringing, maps redrawn. Bram stands in it as a foreigner: he knows its history from books but not his heart, and only Tam carries the memories of their valley life for both of them. Serah, now a defector, brings word that other erased places wait. Emotional beat: bittersweet belonging—home regained, at the cost of remembering why it mattered.
